# /release-baseline

**Purpose:** turn "a batch of merged changes" into a named, verified, rollback-able product version. The ONLY sanctioned path to a release tag.

**Inputs:** all PRs of the batch merged to `main`; their change folders archived; the target environment reachable; the project's semver rules.

**Steps:**
1. Verify preconditions: no open PR belonging to the batch; no active change intended for this release; working tree clean.
2. `git checkout main && git pull`.
3. Deploy: `<project deploy command>`. (Use the environment-appropriate command — production vs local dev may differ; a frontend-only release may just confirm the build/hot-reload.)
4. Migrate: `<run DB migrations>`. Confirm the migration log.
5. Smoke check: `<smoke checklist>` — at minimum a health endpoint plus one primary end-to-end business flow. Record PASS/FAIL in the state snapshot.
6. Decide the version per the project's semver rules (MINOR = batch of features; PATCH = hotfix). The **product** semver is independent from the Syntheprise Framework **kit** `VERSION` file — do not conflate them.
7. Update `CHANGELOG.md` (Keep-a-Changelog): move items from `Unreleased` into a new `vX.Y.Z — YYYY-MM-DD` section.
8. **STOP — owner confirm**, then `git tag vX.Y.Z && git push --tags` (protected action per the safety rules).
9. Record the rollback point in the new state snapshot: previous tag + checkout-previous-tag + rebuild procedure.

**Output:** git tag `vX.Y.Z` on `main`, updated `CHANGELOG.md`, smoke-check evidence + rollback point in `docs/_states/`.

**Forbidden:** tagging without smoke-check evidence; tagging while a change of the batch is un-archived; editing an existing tag (make a new PATCH release instead); pushing tags without owner confirmation.
